name: dsh-vim
description: Vim-style keyboard scrolling (d = down, e = up) for whichever pane the pointer is over — the conversation or the sidebar — a message box that never takes focus on its own (space puts the caret in it, and takes it back out while the box is empty), a choice of what a bare Enter does in the composer (sends, breaks the line, does nothing, or sends on a double Enter — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter always sends, and the composer's own dock row says which), a reasoning-level stepper (q), a model picker (w) that opens a small window listing your chosen models with every reasoning level each one publishes beside it — d / e to move between models, Tab to move between levels, w again to switch, Escape to cancel — plus a task window (f) that answers what is waiting on you before where things live: a block for everything whose ball is in your court (an approval, a plan review, a question, or a run you have not looked at yet) ordered longest-waiting first, a dimmed block for turns in flight, then the last three hours in plain time order (measured across the whole pool, so a run in flight still counts as activity; when the window is genuinely empty the block says Earlier rather than Recent and falls back to the newest batch) — a folder is a label on each row rather than a container around rows, so a busy folder can no longer starve a quiet one out of the list; the attention blocks are read off the whole pool so a debt older than the recency window cannot hide behind the More seat, each row is listed once, and the headline says so in words when nothing needs you; the window opens on the first thing waiting on you so dealing with one row makes the next press land on the next, a running turn's clock counts in whole minutes and stays quiet under the first one, each row leads with its state chip and then the folder and name, so the eye reads what it is doing before it reads which conversation, the just-finished chip pulses once when the window opens so the eye lands on it, and the More seat can be walked onto and confirmed with d / e and the open key — a click outside either window closes it, Escape still does, and the click itself still reaches the page, a pin key (i) that puts the conversation on screen onto the board from the conversation itself, and in the task window puts the row the cursor stands on there — the board only keeps what moved today, and the ★ that outlives that boundary used to be reachable only from a card still on it — a board of goals rather than workspaces: each panel starts as a workspace and takes the name the reader gives it (the ⋯ beside the heading names it; clearing the name restores the workspace's own), and a goal outlives the conversations that filed it so a card pulled out of it has somewhere to go back to; a session card in two columns, four fifths what it says (a title, a two-line note in smaller type, the state chip and its facts) and one fifth the ways to act on it (a drawn enter mark and a drawn branch mark, the same strokes the shell uses, rather than the word 进入 in the smallest type on the card), a live turn's frame marching in dashes, a completion the reader has not looked at yet getting one warm beat, and the card last pressed drawn on top of the pile; a card that can be dragged out of its goal to stand on the paper as a card of its own — where it stands is remembered, and dropping it on any goal puts it back — and idea cards whose width is fixed while their height is the lines they hold, a field that is exactly as tall as the words in it while it is typed into, and a done mark the reader can press; and on the board every card leads its meta line with the same state chip the task window's rows carry (waiting on you outranks running, which outranks just finished), so the board answers what each conversation is doing as well as where it lives; the board is also a sidebar page beside Plugins and Automation, drawn as a canvas: one panel per goal in play today, its conversations stacked under it, and the inbox as a panel of its own — a panel starts out as a workspace but is the reader's to name from the ⋯ beside its heading, and to move by pressing anywhere on it, so it usually ends up being the thing being worked toward; a conversation card is two columns, four fifths of it the title, the pinned line and the state row, one fifth an icon rail holding the way in (an arrow into a frame) above the way to branch (two commits and the line between them), a card whose turn is in flight wears a marching dashed frame, and a card whose completion has not been looked at yet beats once as it is drawn; dragging a card onto another panel files the conversation there, and letting go on the paper gives it a goal of its own named after the one it left — a conversation always belongs to a goal; a goal stands as tall as its conversations, laid out whole with nothing scrolling inside the panel, so the paper is sized from what the painted panels measure and the canvas is the one scroller, and anything new placed on it — a goal stood from the toolbar, a card written from the heading, a workspace arriving mid-board — steps over a tall panel's measured bottom rather than one grid row below its top; an idea card is a piece of paper as tall as what it says - four lines folded on the canvas, ten while its field is open - with a 17px done box in its heading and the whole card as the way into its field; one press handler decides what every press means, by the nearest element that declares itself a handle (card, note, goal, or the paper), and a press that does not travel four pixels is a click for the control under it; panels are dragged by their headings, bare paper is dragged to pan the canvas, tidy answers in one press: every idea card tied to nothing is put away in the inbox as a line that can still be dragged back out, and the goals and the inbox are packed into rows of equal gaps that fill the reader's window, each row clearing the tallest panel above it and the tray closing the flow, while a thought tied to a conversation that is not on the canvas still gets the column beside the tray, a fork is drawn as an indented child under its parent with a line joining them when this client watched the fork (ordinary forks carry no durable parent in the session log, so older branches are shown as roots rather than guessed), entering happens only through each card's Enter button while pressing the card's name renames it in place instead of navigating, and loose text cards can be written anywhere on the canvas, dragged freely and deleted; the paper zooms from a −/100%/＋ control and with Ctrl/Cmd + wheel around the pointer, and a fit mark beside them scales the whole canvas to the window - never magnifying past 100%, and following a resized window until a hand takes the scale back, each panel carries the notes tied to its conversations while it is dragged, and the ties are cubic curves measured again on every frame of a drag, with a snapped note gliding into its margin rather than jumping;  a card dropped on a conversation is tied to it by a measured line and snapped into the margin beside its panel, while a card dropped on that conversation's Enter button opens it and pastes the card's words into the composer as a draft (never sending), names the conversation after the card's own title - the hand-over is the one deliberate moment a name is given to work, a tie or a filing names nothing, and a refusal leaves the name it had - and stays behind as a greyed, dashed-line trace marked done; the running chip carries its own clock, ticking in place once a minute, and a status tick that changes no card's word costs no repaint; and notes are written on the board itself: a card's note mark opens a field inside the card, Enter keeps the line, Escape drops it, and a press elsewhere keeps it too; pressing the line again edits it and emptying it takes it away, while the note key (n) opens the board on the conversation on screen with that card's field already waiting — the lines are stored apart from the board's own arrangement, so a board reset cannot cost the reader a thought; a session card that is a way in rather than a picture of one — a press anywhere on it opens the conversation, its name included, while renaming has a mark of its own that steps forward only under the pointer and takes no width from the card, so a host write is never one stray click away, and the enter arrow stays as the second way in and as the drop target a dragged idea card is let go on; a branch cut from a card no longer inherits its parent's name unchanged — once the child lands the board settles its name against the whole list, says which name it got, and stops answering its own branch mark until that answer arrives, so two impatient presses cannot make two identically named children; and two cards that still share a name each say where they stand among their namesakes; a finished-cards bin in the board's heading — a chip that says how many it holds and opens into the same one-line rows the inbox uses, where a finished idea card handed to its conversation is kept (the card leaves the canvas, the list keeps a line saying which conversation it was handed to), the press saying how many it put away and offering one press to undo it, and a card taken out of the bin by dragging a row back onto the canvas or by un-checking it - which puts it back on the paper at once, because a bin called done that keeps unfinished work is lying about its own name; idea cards as one line of opaque paper that hides what is under it, grown by a corner grip to as many lines as the reader wants and remembering that height, the sentence about which conversation it belongs to replaced by a dot in that conversation's goal colour, and the unlink turned into a drawn icon; twelve colour seats shared out between goals by their own ids and spread apart, so renaming a panel cannot change its colour and two goals never wear two blues, with the notes tied to a goal taking its paper and the ones that belong to nobody keeping the amber; and the finished-cards bin reachable from each conversation card's own archive mark (drawn only when it holds something) as well as from the heading, which keeps out of the way while it is empty, and a session row dragged in from the host's own sidebar lands on the board as a card: the shell's rows are natively draggable — the same gesture the list is reordered by — and what a row carries is its conversation's id, so the canvas draws the goal that would take it while the hand is still over the paper, letting go puts the conversation on the board under the goal it was aimed at (or the one its workspace gives it) and sets the mark that outlives the day the way the pin key does, while a drag that was not a conversation is refused with a word rather than taken silently, and a right press on the conversation is the way back — the one button its page never used: the shell keeps its context menus in the sidebar and the transcript answers a right press with nothing, so the button becomes the shortest path back to the board, taken only from the conversation's own marked body and never from the box being typed into or from inside a text selection, where a right press still means copy, and a goal's heading carries a plus that starts a new conversation there: a press opens a sheet that asks for a title and a body, puts the body in the new conversation's message box as a draft and names the conversation from the title, a title with no body making the conversation and opening it with nothing said yet, a model row that opens the page's own model window and lands the chosen model on the conversation before its first message goes out, while an idea card dropped on the same plus starts one from the card's own words and stays behind as a finished trace; a goal's row of conversations stops at three and starts another row under it, so a busy goal grows downward instead of running off the paper, and the conversations the day merely carried in - nothing touched, nothing running, nothing marked - are drawn as the quiet strip at the foot of the panel rather than a column apiece: one line reading how many are quiet and how long the oldest has waited, unfolding on a press into a line per conversation, each line still the way in and still carrying a count of its thoughts that puts them back on the paper, with no mark to earn and none to undo because a quiet conversation is a column again the moment it moves, is marked, or starts a turn, and a panel's own count counts only the ones it is working in
